title: Land Cover Datasets
description: Global land cover and canopy height rasters at 100 m (CGLS-LC100 2019 land cover classification) and 10 m (ETH 2020 canopy top height with uncertainty), provided as Cloud-Optimized GeoTIFFs/VRTs and as H3 resolution-9 hex GeoParquet layers. Land cover uses 23 FAO LCCS classes with ~80% overall accuracy; canopy height is a deep learning model trained on GEDI lidar and Sentinel-2 imagery.

## README.md
# Copernicus Global Land Cover 100 m v3.0.1 (CGLS-LC100, 2019)

Global land cover classification at 100 m resolution for 2019, from the
[Copernicus Global Land Service Land Cover product v3.0.1 (Collection 3)](https://land.copernicus.eu/global/products/lc).
Uses the FAO Land Cover Classification System (LCCS); overall accuracy ~80%.

License: **CC-BY-4.0**. Source: <https://zenodo.org/records/3939050>.

## Assets

| Asset | Format | Path |
|---|---|---|
| `cgls-lc100-2019-cog` | Cloud-Optimized GeoTIFF (EPSG:4326, uint8) | `https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-land-cover/cgls-lc100-2019-cog.tif` |
| `cgls-lc100-2019-hex` | H3 hex GeoParquet (resolution 9, hive-partitioned by `h0`) | `https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-land-cover/cgls-lc100-2019/hex/h0=*/data_0.parquet` |

The hex layer aggregates the source raster to **H3 resolution 9** (~174 m edge,
~10 source pixels per cell) by **mode** (most frequent class per cell). One row per
`h9` cell. `lc_class` is **categorical** — only the 23 canonical LCCS codes appear.
Re-hexed on the antimeridian/polar-fixed pipeline (boettiger-lab/datasets #88, #92,
#93); the prior resolution-8 build inflated and dropped cells at the ±180° seam
(boettiger-lab/data-workflows #186).

## Querying the hex layer (DuckDB)

```sql
INSTALL httpfs; LOAD httpfs;
-- Global class histogram (cell counts)
SELECT lc_class, COUNT(*) AS cells
FROM read_parquet('https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-land-cover/cgls-lc100-2019/hex/h0=*/data_0.parquet')
GROUP BY lc_class ORDER BY cells DESC;
```

`lc_class` is a class code — **never `SUM` or `AVG` it.** To estimate the area of a
class, count distinct cells and multiply by the H3 resolution-9 cell area:

```sql
-- Approx area (km²) of forest classes (111–126), res-9 cell ≈ 0.105 km²
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT h9) * 0.105 AS forest_km2
FROM read_parquet('https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-land-cover/cgls-lc100-2019/hex/h0=*/data_0.parquet')
WHERE lc_class BETWEEN 111 AND 126;
```

Parent indexes `h8`, `h7`, `h6`, `h5` are present for multi-scale joins; partition on
`h0` to prune reads.

## Displaying the COG (MapLibre GL JS via TiTiler)

The raster has no PMTiles layer; render the COG through a TiTiler XYZ endpoint:

```js
map.addSource('cgls-lc100', {
  type: 'raster',
  tiles: ['https://titiler.../cog/tiles/{z}/{x}/{y}.png?url=' +
    encodeURIComponent('https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-land-cover/cgls-lc100-2019-cog.tif') +
    '&colormap_name=...'],   // use the categorical class palette (see classification:classes in STAC)
  tileSize: 256
});
map.addLayer({ id: 'cgls-lc100', type: 'raster', source: 'cgls-lc100' });
```

## Land cover classes (FAO LCCS)

| Code | Class | | Code | Class |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | No input data | | 113 | Closed forest, deciduous needle leaf |
| 20 | Shrubs | | 114 | Closed forest, deciduous broad leaf |
| 30 | Herbaceous vegetation | | 115 | Closed forest, mixed |
| 40 | Cultivated / managed | | 116 | Closed forest, unknown |
| 50 | Urban / built-up | | 121 | Open forest, evergreen needle leaf |
| 60 | Bare / sparse vegetation | | 122 | Open forest, evergreen broad leaf |
| 70 | Snow and ice | | 123 | Open forest, deciduous needle leaf |
| 80 | Permanent water bodies | | 124 | Open forest, deciduous broad leaf |
| 90 | Herbaceous wetland | | 125 | Open forest, mixed |
| 100 | Moss and lichen | | 126 | Open forest, unknown |
| 111 | Closed forest, evergreen needle leaf | | 200 | Open sea |

Value 0 ("No input data") is a retained fill class; the COG GDAL NoData sentinel is 255.

## Global canopy height 2020, 10 m (`canopy-height-2020`)

Canopy top height for 2020 at 10 m, 60 S to 84 N, from Lang et al. (2023, ETH Zurich): a deep learning model trained on GEDI lidar and applied to Sentinel-2 imagery. It comes with the model's predictive standard deviation, a per-pixel uncertainty. Built-up areas, snow, ice and permanent water are masked (255).

| Asset | URL |
|---|---|
| Height, 10 m (VRT over 2,651 COG tiles) | `https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-land-cover/canopy-height-2020/height.vrt` |
| Standard deviation, 10 m (VRT) | `https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-land-cover/canopy-height-2020/sd.vrt` |
| H3 hex, mean height (resolution 9) | `https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-land-cover/canopy-height-2020/height/hex/h0=*/data_0.parquet` |
| H3 hex, mean standard deviation (resolution 9) | `https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-land-cover/canopy-height-2020/sd/hex/h0=*/data_0.parquet` |
| STAC | `https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-land-cover/canopy-height-2020/stac-collection.json` |

The VRTs index the producers' own 3-degree cloud-optimized GeoTIFF tiles (in `height/tiles/` and `sd/tiles/`) with relative paths, so GDAL opens them over https or S3. Heights are whole metres; values above about 80 m are artefacts (a handful of cells, mostly at high latitude). The standard deviation hex is the average of the per-pixel standard deviations, which is an upper bound on the uncertainty of a cell's mean height, not that uncertainty itself.

### DuckDB

```sql
-- mean canopy height per resolution 8 cell, tallest first: the plain average of its resolution 9
-- cells with data (a partly masked cell counts as much as a fully covered one)
SELECT h8, AVG(canopy_height_m) AS height_m
FROM read_parquet('https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-land-cover/canopy-height-2020/height/hex/h0=*/data_0.parquet')
GROUP BY h8 ORDER BY height_m DESC LIMIT 10;
```

### MapLibre GL JS

```js
map.addSource("canopy-height", {
  type: "raster",
  tiles: ["https://titiler.nrp-nautilus.io/cog/tiles/WebMercatorQuad/{z}/{x}/{y}.png?url=https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-land-cover/canopy-height-2020/height.vrt&rescale=0,50&colormap_name=viridis"],
  tileSize: 256,
});
map.addLayer({ id: "canopy-height", type: "raster", source: "canopy-height" });
```

### Source and licence

Lang, N., Jetz, W., Schindler, K., & Wegner, J. D. (2023). A high-resolution canopy height model of the Earth. *Nature Ecology & Evolution*, https://doi.org/10.1038/s41559-023-02206-6. Data: ETH Global Canopy Height 2020, version 1, https://doi.org/10.3929/ethz-b-000609802, downloaded 2026-10-29 from the producers' share (https://langnico.github.io/globalcanopyheight/); tiles are published unchanged, with sizes and sha256 in `s3://public-land-cover/raw/canopy-height-2020/manifest/`. **CC BY 4.0**.
